body:
Our garage door advice guides answer the questions homeowners ask us most often: how much garage doors cost, which type is best, whether roller doors are secure, and what to do when an electric door stops working. They are written in plain English to help you make a good decision, whether or not you end up using us.

If you are buying a new garage door

Start with types of garage doors in the UK, which compares up and over, roller, sectional and side hinged doors side by side. Then read choosing the best garage door for advice on matching a door to your home and budget, and garage door sizes in the UK so you understand standard sizes and how openings are measured.

Other useful buying guides include:

  • What garage doors are made of — steel, timber, GRP, aluminium and composite compared
  • Are insulated garage doors worth it? — when insulation makes a real difference
  • Garage conversion doors — options if you are turning a garage into living space

How much do garage doors cost?

This is the question we are asked more than any other. Our electric garage door cost guide explains what drives the price of automatic doors, and our garage door prices page gives indicative fitted price ranges for each door type. Both make it clear that exact prices depend on your opening and are confirmed after a free survey.

Security and insurance

Garages often hold bikes, tools and cars, and an integral garage can be a way into the house. Read are roller garage doors secure?, our practical guide on how to secure a garage door, and our guide to whether home insurance covers garage doors to understand where you stand.

Maintenance, repairs and troubleshooting

A little care goes a long way. Our garage door maintenance guide covers safe checks you can do yourself, and our lifespan guide explains how long garage doors typically last. If something has gone wrong, see electric garage door not working and our guide to repairing versus replacing a garage door.

Safety first: garage door springs and cables are under high tension and can cause serious injury. Our guides never include DIY spring adjustment. If you suspect a spring or cable problem, stop using the door and call a professional.

Where to start

Pick the question closest to yours and start there.

  • Choosing a new door: types of garage doors, the best garage doors in the UK, materials and sizes.
  • Costs: electric garage door costs, whether insulation is worth it and our full price guide.
  • Security: are roller doors secure?, how to secure your garage and home insurance and garage doors.
  • Problems: electric door not working, repair or replace and how long doors last.
  • Upkeep and projects: maintenance, painting, seals and condensation, how roller doors work and garage conversions.

Need help with something specific?

If a guide doesn't answer your question, get in touch. Our engineers in Milton Keynes are happy to give advice over the phone, and if you need a repair or new door you can request a free quote. All our guides are listed below.

faqs.q: How much are garage doors in the UK?
faqs.a: As a broad guide, a manual steel up and over door typically costs around £750–£1,400 fitted, while insulated electric roller and sectional doors are often £1,600–£3,800 fitted. Timber, bespoke and double doors cost more. These are indicative ranges; see our garage door prices page and get a free survey for an exact figure.

Garage doors are best repaired by a specialist garage door engineer rather than a general handyman, because springs, cables and motors need specific knowledge and tools. Look for someone who repairs all major makes, explains the fault clearly and gives you a price before starting. Our garage door repairs page explains what we cover.

faqs.q: Can I repair my garage door myself?
faqs.a: Some simple jobs are fine for a confident DIYer, such as cleaning tracks, lubricating hinges and rollers, replacing remote batteries or tightening loose fixings. Anything involving springs, cables or the tension system should be left to a professional, because these parts store a lot of energy and can cause serious injury if released.

faqs.q: Who writes these garage door guides?
faqs.a: Our guides are researched and written by Muhammad Usman Siddiqui, who looks after this website and its advice content. They draw on manufacturer information and the practical questions homeowners in Milton Keynes ask us. You can read more on our about page.
